page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX and AVX-512F. The instance is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB per core.

Acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, featuring 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between CPU-bound workloads and GPU-accelerated tasks. Standard CPU performance is relatively modest, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is weak, though large block read and write operations reach average tiers. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance in machine learning workloads. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing speeds, reaching 8407.18 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 1134.43 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are average to strong, with the 7B model achieving 33.96 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents an entry-level GPU tier. It trades raw CPU performance and local storage for affordable access to hardware acceleration. This resource profile makes the instance highly suitable for lightweight deep learning inference, small-to-medium language model execution, and GPU-accelerated video transcoding, while it is less optimal for CPU-heavy compilation, high-throughput web serving, or memory-intensive database operations.

Built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor, this instance lacks local storage and relies on a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate weak general-purpose CPU and memory performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores in the bottom 25%. However, the integrated Turing-architecture GPU excels at machine learning tasks, delivering top-tier prompt processing speeds of 1134.43 tokens per second on 7B LLM models and strong text generation performance. This qualitative balance makes the instance a cost-effective choice for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-to-medium model inference and media processing, rather than CPU-bound or storage-heavy applications.
